Prevention: Remove weeds in and around the field to reduce overwintering population.
Irrigate less, but more often to interfere with pupation.
Monitoring: Monitoring should be conducted after seedlings appear, using blue boards. 10 blue boards per mu.
Blue boards should be hung 10-20cm above the crops and adjusted as the crop grows.
Check flowers and leaves at early flowering stage (5 monitoring sites per field; check at least 2 crops per site); direct control should be conducted once thrips appear.
Direct Control: Remove infected leaves and bury them outside the field.
Lure and kill using blue boards as described in monitoring section.
Bio-control: apply predatory mites ( Amblyseius barkeri or
Neoseiulus cucumeris oudermans ); 20000 mites per mu, one release each month.
Chemical pesticides should be avoided 7 days before and during the release.
Sex pheromone traps: combining sex pheromone traps onto blue boards can trap thrips better.
Restrictions: Chemical pesticides must be applied strictly according to the prescribed dosages to avoid residue problems.
Rotational application of pesticides to avoid resistance.
PPEs is mandatory while using chemical pesticides.
WHO U, Maximum 3 sprays during each growing season, Spray when thrips population is high, PHI: 3 days.
